source_text:
Σπουδάζετε οὖν βεβαιωθῆναι ἐν τοῖς δόγμασιν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων, ἵνα πάντα, ὅσα ποιεῖτε, κατευοδωθῆτε σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι, πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἐν υἱῷ καὶ πατρὶ καὶ ἐν πνεύματι, ἐν ἀρχῇ καὶ ἐν τέλει, μετὰ τοῦ ἀξιοπρεπεστάτου ἐπισκόπου ὑμῶν καὶ ἀξιοπλόκου πνευματικοῦ στεφάνου τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν κατὰ θεὸν διακόνων.
ὑποτάγητε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ ἀλλήλοις, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῷ πατρὶ ἵνα ἕνωσις ᾖ σαρκική τε καὶ πνευματική.
thought_title: Be established in the Lord's teachings and submit to the bishop
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, urging them to be confirmed in the teachings of the Lord and the apostles and to submit to the bishop and one another.
pass_a_gloss: Be eager therefore to be established in the teachings of the Lord and of the apostles, in order that all [things], as many as you do, you may prosper in flesh and in spirit, in faith and in love, in Son and in Father and in Spirit, in beginning and in end, with your most worthy bishop and the well-woven spiritual crown of your council of elders and the deacons according to God. Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ [was subject] to the Father and the apostles [were subject] to Christ and to the Father, in order that unity may be fleshly and spiritual.

choices.why: The glossary does not cover this term; 'teachings' fits the context of instruction from the Lord and apostles better than 'decrees' or 'doctrines,' which sound more formal or legalistic.
The verb means to have a good journey or to succeed; 'prosper' captures the sense of thriving in all that they do, in both flesh and spirit.
rejected: be led on a good path

choices.why: The metaphor of a woven crown for the council of elders is vivid; 'well-woven' preserves the compound adjective's force and the image of unity.
The glossary uses 'submit' for the concept of submission to the bishop, but the imperative here is passive; 'be subject' keeps the passive force and matches the parallel with Christ and the apostles.
The unity is described with two adjectives; 'fleshly' is chosen over 'bodily' to match the glossary's 'flesh' for σάρξ and to preserve the contrast with 'spiritual.'

pass_b_english: Make every effort, then, to be established in the teachings of the Lord and the apostles, so that you may prosper in everything you do, in flesh and spirit, in faith and love, in the Son and the Father and in the Spirit, in beginning and in end, together with your most worthy bishop and the well-woven spiritual crown of your council of elders and the deacons who serve according to God.

Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ was subject to the Father and the apostles were subject to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a unity that is both fleshly and spiritual.
